## Problem

`proxy/proxy/handlers.py:489` carries a `# noqa` comment whose text is prose
rather than a comma-separated code list, so ruff cannot parse it as a
suppression. Every `ruff check` run in this repo — repo-wide or file-scoped —
prints a warning to stderr:

```
$ ruff check --select I001 proxy/proxy/handlers.py
warning: Invalid `# noqa` directive on proxy/proxy/handlers.py:489: expected a
comma-separated list of codes (e.g. `# noqa: F401, F841`).
All checks passed!
```

Current source:

```python
    import os  # noqa: local import for config access
```

## Why it matters

- The comment gives no suppression at all: whatever it was intended to silence
  (`F401`? a local-import / `PLC0415` style rule?) is either already allowed by
  `.ruff.toml` or silently expressed as prose — so the intent is unrecoverable
  from the code.
- It makes every lint invocation in this repository noisy, which trains readers
  and agents to ignore ruff's warning channel — the exact channel that would
  surface a genuinely broken suppression.
- It was noted as a known-but-out-of-scope side observation while clearing the
  `I001` findings of epic `LP-0MVLK5H04003FZJS` (see
  `LP-0MVKE61H9001WPAQ` for the earlier sighting).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — warning cleared:** `python3 -m ruff check proxy/proxy/handlers.py`
      produces no `Invalid \`noqa\` directive` warning and still reports
      `All checks passed!` (command + output captured on the work item).
- [ ] **AC2 — intent preserved:** the reason for the directive is expressed
      either as a valid code list (e.g. `# noqa: PLC0415`) that matches the
      rule actually triggered, or as a plain explanatory comment with no
      `noqa` prefix. Determined by removing the directive and re-running ruff
      on the file to see which rule (if any) fires; recorded in the closure
      comment.
- [ ] **AC3 — no blanket suppression:** `.ruff.toml` gains no new
      `per-file-ignores`/global `ignore` entry for `proxy/proxy/handlers.py`,
      so genuine future findings remain detectable (`git diff --stat` on
      `.ruff.toml` empty for this item).
- [ ] **AC4 — no behaviour change:** the change is comment-only; the
      `import os` statement itself is untouched, so runtime behaviour is
      identical.
- [ ] **AC5 — full suite green:** validation runs through the test skill
      (`/skill:test`, changed scope at the implement gate, full suite at the
      dev-push gate) — no ad-hoc `pytest`.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — line 489 holds the invalid directive
  (`import os  # noqa: local import for config access`).
- `.ruff.toml` — **must remain unchanged**; no suppression may be added.

## Provenance

Discovered from: `LP-0MVLK5H04003FZJS` (Quality Improvement - Refactoring epic) while
closing child `LP-0MVMLII27004JVII` — that item verified
`ruff check --select I001 .` clean at HEAD `9db15857` and this stray `# noqa`
warning was the only remaining lint-channel noise observed. Earlier sighting
recorded in `LP-0MVKE61H9001WPAQ`. Not blocking that epic: the epic tracks
`I001` findings, and this is a distinct (pre-existing) hygiene defect.
data.title: invalid noqa directive at proxy/proxy/handlers.py:489 makes every ruff run warn (discovered-from LP-0MVLK5H04003FZJS)

## Goal

As the proxy operator I want one INFO log line per compaction-header emission
(and one distinguishable line when compaction was evaluated but emitted
nothing), so that reading the proxy log tells me whether the signal was
emitted at all — closing secondary finding 2 of the parent ("Header emission
logs nothing ... a loaded-but-idle extension is indistinguishable from a broken
one") and satisfying AC4's proxy half.

Parent: LP-0MVWBFN8L004Z3X8. Unconditional — this is required whether or not
Phase A/B pass.

## Current state (verified during planning)

- `proxy/proxy/router.py:397` `_build_compaction_headers()` returns `{}` or the
  header dict; the only log statement in it is
  `logger.debug("Failed to build compaction headers; omitting", ...)` on the
  exception path (`router.py:430`). The success path logs nothing.
- `router.py:2336` applies it with `outgoing_headers.update(...)` on the
  streaming path; a second site near `router.py:3551` covers the buffered path.
- `router_helpers.py:6218` already logs `session_compaction applied
  session=… priority=… est_before=… est_after=…` — but that line proves
  *compaction happened*, not that *headers were emitted*. The two can diverge
  (e.g. `compaction_summary_text` empty → no headers, compaction still
  applied).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: On the live-applied path, exactly one INFO line per response is logged:
  `compaction_headers emitted session=<id8> turns_summarized=<n>
  recent_turns_kept=<k> marker_chars=<len>`. It is logged once per response on
  both the streaming (SSE) and buffered response paths — never once per SSE
  chunk.
- AC2: A response that evaluated compaction but emitted no headers logs exactly
  one line naming the reason, distinguishable from "emitted": one of
  `compaction_headers none reason=disabled|below_trigger|noop|dry_run|
  remote_with_guidance|no_summary_text|build_failed`. `no_summary_text` covers
  the real divergence case (compaction applied, summary missing) and
  `build_failed` covers the exception path.
- AC3: No header-emission line is emitted for requests that never reach the
  compaction path (e.g. remote dispatch with no session), keeping router log
  volume unchanged for the overwhelmingly common `compaction_disabled` case at
  a rate that permits long-window analysis (the `session_compaction applied`
  line already fires per compacted request; the new line must not multiply
  log volume for non-compaction traffic).
- AC4: The fail-safe contract is unchanged and better observed: an exception
  while building headers still yields no headers and never changes dispatch,
  but is now logged at **WARNING** with `exc_info=True` (was `debug`), so a
  silently broken emission is visible in normal operation.
- AC5: Header names, values and encodings are untouched:
  `proxy/tests/test_compaction_headers_contract.py` passes **unmodified**.
- AC6: Unit tests assert: the AC1 line and each field on both response paths;
  exactly one AC1 line per response with a multi-chunk SSE stream; the AC2
  reason line for `disabled` / `below_trigger` / `dry_run` /
  `remote_with_guidance` / `no_summary_text`; WARNING + `exc_info` on the
  exception path; and that a logging failure cannot raise out of the emission
  path (fail-safe preserved).
- AC7: No marker text, no summary body and no message content appear in any
  log line — only ids, counts and lengths.
- (Parent AC4) the proxy logs one INFO per header emission (session, `turns_summarized`, `recent_turns_kept`, marker length) and the bridge logs one line per signal capture and one per reshape. A reader of the logs can tell "no signal emitted" from "signal emitted, bridge ignored it".

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a module-level helper in `proxy/proxy/router.py` next to
  `_build_compaction_headers` — e.g. `_log_compaction_headers(session_id,
  headers, reason=None)` — and call it from the two `outgoing_headers.update(
  _build_compaction_headers(...))` sites, so the accounting is in one place
  and both paths are testable with the existing `_mock_upstream_response`
  fixtures.
- Derive `reason` where the decision is already known rather than re-deriving
  it: `_build_compaction_headers` can return `(headers, reason)` internally
  while keeping its public single-dict behaviour, or the caller can read
  `session_result["compaction_reason"]` / `compaction_applied`. Prefer the
  minimal change that does not alter the contract test's public seam.
- Session id is already available at both call sites (`session_id`); truncate
  to 8 chars like the existing `session_compaction applied` line does, so
  operator greps work across both lines.
- `marker_chars` is `len(marker_b64)` (the header value length), which is what
  the parent's AC4 asks for ("marker length").

## Deliverables

- Emission telemetry in `proxy/proxy/router.py` on both response paths.
- Unit tests in `proxy/tests/test_compaction_headers_contract.py` (extend) or
  a new `proxy/tests/test_compaction_headers_telemetry.py` (preferred: keeps the
  frozen contract file untouched per AC5).

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/router.py`
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_headers_contract.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_headers_telemetry.py`
- `docs/session-compaction-design.md`

## Dependencies

None. Required by the T1 execution child (its pass criteria C/D are read from
these lines) and by the parent's AC4.
data.title: Proxy INFO telemetry on every compaction header emission

data.description:
## Goal

As the proxy operator I want the client-side bridge to log one line per
captured compaction signal and one line per reshape attempt, so that a
loaded-but-idle extension (bridge installed, no signal ever arrives) is
distinguishable from a broken one (signal arrived, bridge did nothing) —
satisfying AC4's client half and making the parent's pass criterion D
(ordering evidence) observable.

Parent: LP-0MVWBFN8L004Z3X8. Unconditional — required whether or not Phase B
passes.

## Cross-repo constraint (read first)

This work lands in the **SorraAgents** repository, not this one:

- code: `~/projects/SorraAgents/pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/`
  (`index.ts` adapter + `compaction-bridge.js` pure core),
- tests: `~/projects/SorraAgents/tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs`,
- loaded via the symlink `~/.pi/agent/extensions/proxy-compaction-bridge` →
  that directory (verified present 2026-10-31), so no reinstall is needed
  beyond `/reload` inside pi.

The commit hash in SorraAgents must be recorded on this child and on the
parent, so the client half of AC4 is traceable from the LP item. Do not copy
the bridge into this repository.

## Current state (verified during planning)

- `compaction-bridge.js` has no logging at all: `handleResponse` returns a
  boolean, `reshape` returns a list or `null`. Neither reports why.
- `index.ts` wires `after_provider_response` and `context` and silently
  returns on a stale ctx / missing signal.
- There is no `ctx.ui` in print or JSON mode (`docs/extensions.md`), so
  `ctx.ui.notify` cannot be the logging channel — headless T2 would lose it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: One line per **captured** signal, emitted from the pure core:
  `compaction-bridge signal captured session=<id8> turns_summarized=<n>
  recent_turns_kept=<k> marker_chars=<len>`.
- AC2: One line per **reshape attempt**:
  - applied: `compaction-bridge reshaped <X>-><Y> messages session=<id8>`
    with `Y < X`,
  - not applicable: `compaction-bridge no signal — passthrough session=<id8>`
    (state absent) — the "loaded but idle" line, and
  - anomalous signal (fewer turns than `turnsSummarized`):
    `compaction-bridge reshape refused reason=insufficient_turns session=<id8>`.
- AC3: Exactly one line per event: `handleResponse` logs once whether or not a
  signal was parsed (no-signal case logs at most once per response, and is
  rate-limited to one line per session per turn so an idle session does not
  spam), and `reshape` logs once per `context` event.
- AC4: Works in every pi mode (interactive, RPC, JSON, print): no `ctx.ui`
  dependency. Lines go to **stderr** and, when
  `PROXY_COMPACTION_BRIDGE_LOG` is set, are appended to that file, one line
  each. The default channel and the optional file path are documented in the
  extension README.
- AC5: No marker text, no message content and no summary body in any line —
  session id (truncated to 8), counts and lengths only.
- AC6: Logging never changes behaviour and never throws: the logger is
  injected into `createCompactionBridge({ log })` with a no-op default, so the
  pure module stays dependency-free and a hostile/throwing logger leaves
  parse/reshape results identical.
- AC7: `tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs` extended to assert: the AC1 line
  and its fields; the AC2 applied / passthrough / refused lines; the AC3
  one-line-per-event rule including the idle no-spam case; the AC5 no-body
  guarantee (assert the marker string does not appear in any captured line);
  and AC6 (identical `parseCompactionSignal` / `reshapeContext` results with a
  no-op logger vs a throwing logger). All pre-existing bridge tests stay green
  unmodified.
- AC8: README documents the exact log lines, the `PROXY_COMPACTION_BRIDGE_LOG`
  variable, and the grep recipe used by T2's criterion D.
- (Parent AC4) the proxy logs one INFO per header emission (session, `turns_summarized`, `recent_turns_kept`, marker length) and the bridge logs one line per signal capture and one per reshape. A reader of the logs can tell "no signal emitted" from "signal emitted, bridge ignored it".

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a `log` option to `createCompactionBridge({ log } = {})` defaulting to a
  no-op; the default writer lives in `index.ts` (adapter layer), keeping
  `compaction-bridge.js` free of `fs`/`process` imports except behind an
  injected function.
- Emit from inside `handleResponse` / `reshape` where the decision is already
  made — no re-parsing, no extra state.
- Idle rate-limiting is one `Set` of session ids already logged for
  passthrough, cleared when a signal is captured for that session (keeps the
  module dependency-free and the logic pure).
- Keep the existing public surface (`handleResponse` boolean, `reshape` list or
  null) unchanged so `index.ts` and the tests need no behavioural edits.
- Run `node --test` for the extension's unit test only via the test skill
  (`/skill:test` scope) — not ad-hoc.

## Deliverables

- `compaction-bridge.js` telemetry + injected logger.
- `index.ts` default logger wiring (stderr + optional file).
- `README.md` log-line documentation.
- `tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs` extended coverage.
- SorraAgents commit hash recorded on this item.

**Key Files:**

- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/compaction-bridge.js`
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/index.ts`
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/README.md`
- `tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs`

## Dependencies

None. Required by the T2 execution child (pass criterion D reads these lines).

# Extend the status builder's live-work attribution during prefill (72 residual saturated-without-live-work polls)

Follow-on item filed from the **LP-0MVUVHBZH007INL1** verification verdict (2026-11-01 night window), **re-targeted 2026-11-02 after log-analysis evidence corrected the attribution** (see Evidence below).

**Verdict (unchanged):** EXPECTED IMPROVEMENT ACHIEVED: NO — 72 saturated-without-live-work polls (0.41 %) remain, up from the 12-poll / 0.11 % AC4 residual baseline (+60 polls) though down from the 247-poll / 2.12 % pre-fix baseline. The abandoned_busy annotation IS firing (367 polls / 2.06 %), so the shift is real. Of the 72 residual polls, 65 were **tool-attributed** to `session_evicted` (nearest event within the 600 s lookback), 1 to `no_progress_watchdog`, 1 to `prefill_deadline`, and 5 were unattributable (2026-11-01 22:12:58, 22:13:00 ×2, 23:02:37, 23:03:32).

## Problem statement

A slot that is genuinely busy prefilling a real local dispatch reports `capacity_hint=saturated` with empty live-work fields (`local_in_flight_requests=0`, `local_owner_session_id=None`, `local_active_query=false`) on fresh slot detail, so consumers cannot tell the slot is doing live work. The measured residual is 72 polls / 0.41 % of the 2026-11-01 night, all attributable to status-builder attribution lag during prefill rather than to the post-cancel draining-ghost class the abandoned_busy fix (LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM) already closes.

## Evidence (log-analysis, 2026-11-01 night episode 05:26–05:33)

The original "session-eviction path" reading was a **nearest-event mis-attribution** — the eviction was not draining when the residual polls were read:

1. 05:26:46.361 `Evicted 2 expired/invalidated session(s)` → `lease_released` ×2 (`session_evicted`). Both slots were **already free 7 s later**: 05:26:53.850 status reads `available_slots=2`, `capacity_hint=idle`, `in_flight=0`. No draining ghost existed from this eviction.
2. 05:27:10.829 a NEW local dispatch begins: `[local] POST slot=0 session=herdr-1793585223-1761548-25344` (large ~107K-token full-prompt reprocess; lease_extended_during_prefill at 05:27:22/05:28:07/05:28:19) — the slot is genuinely busy with live work.
3. The first residual poll (05:31:18.459) is 6 ms BEFORE `Stream started: provider=local session=herdr-1793596937-2342287-16191 turn=993bed20` (05:31:18.465) + `prefill_progress_measured` (31K tokens) — a second live local dispatch starts at that exact second.
4. All 65 residual polls (05:31:18 → 05:33:07) read `available_slots=1`, `capacity_hint=saturated`, `local_in_flight_requests=0`, `local_owner_session_id=None`, `local_active_query=false`, `slots_detail_stale=false`: a busy slot whose in-flight/owner attribution the status payload does **not** reflect during prefill.
5. Same shape reproduces live (2026-11-02 09:06): `available_slots=1` + `saturated` + `in_flight=0` + `owner=None` for several seconds while slot prefill for a REAL dispatch is in flight (owner + in_flight appear ~9 s later). Also observed: `available_slots=2` + `saturated` with fresh detail (09:06:41) — the counts-stale family (LP-0MVXSX0TZ00798KA).

## Users

- **Proxy operator / on-call.** Reads `/llama/local/status` to decide whether the machine is genuinely busy. A `saturated` hint from a prefilling slot misdirects triage and hides real saturation (alarm fatigue).
- **Routing policy / dispatchers** (including the herdr downtime worker). `saturated` steers work to cloud/remote providers; a false `saturated` from live work causes avoidable paid fallback and, historically, starvation of the downtime dispatcher (LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM).
- **Measurement analyst** re-running `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`. Needs every residual poll attributable, otherwise the next re-measurement is as unexplained as this one.

User stories:

- As an on-call operator, when a slot is prefilling a real local dispatch, I want the status payload to say so (owner/in-flight set), so I don't misread capacity.
- As the herdr downtime worker, when a slot is doing live prefill work, I accept `saturated`; when it is not, I want a signal that distinguishes it, so I don't fall back to paid providers needlessly.
- As a measurement analyst, I want the widened attribution reason set to cover every residual poll, so re-measurements reach zero or full attribution.

## Goal (re-targeted)

Reconcile **slot-occupancy vs in-flight/owner attribution in the status builder** so a slot that is genuinely busy with live local work (prefill in progress for a real dispatch) reads its live-work attribution (`local_in_flight_requests`/`local_owner_session_id`/`local_active_query` or an equivalent signal) instead of `capacity_hint=saturated` with empty live-work fields. This is **NOT** the post-cancel draining-ghost the LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM fix targets — extending `abandoned_busy` to the session-eviction path would not close this class.

## Work

1. Root-cause the status-builder lag: why does a slot prefilling for a real local dispatch read `in_flight=0` / `owner=None` (busy slot, but no live-work attribution)? Check against the counts-stale family LP-0MVXSX0TZ00798KA first (the 09:06:41 `available_slots=2` + `saturated` shape may be the same family).
2. Fix the status builder (or the residual classifier) to attribute live work during prefill — truthful-status contract LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM must not be weakened (`some` live work must still read `saturated`).
3. Re-run the measurement over a comparable night (same invocation shape as `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-11-01_night-post-deploy/run_measurement.sh`) to confirm the residual drops toward 0.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A slot prefilling a real local dispatch never reports `capacity_hint=saturated` with `local_in_flight_requests=0` / empty owner on fresh slot detail; it either carries the live-work attribution or reads a live-work hint.
- AC2: A pool with live work still reads `saturated` (truthful-status contract LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM unweakened) — existing deterministic tests pass unchanged.
- AC3: Over a fresh closed night window, saturated-without-live-work polls are 0, or every residual is attributed with the widened reason set.
- AC4: The 5 unattributable polls from the 2026-11-01 night are either attributed via extended evidence (see LP-0MVVXGMGB004DUGR) or provably absent.

## Constraints

- Truthful-status contract LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM must not be weakened: a pool with live work must still read `saturated` (`some` live work, even unfinalised during prefill, is still live).
- Do not duplicate LP-0MVVXGMGB004DUGR (attribution extension for unattributable polls) — reference it; AC4 here is bounded by "or provably absent".
- Measurement windows must be comparable in invocation shape to the 2026-11-01 night run (`run_measurement.sh`) and free of proxy-process restarts inside the window (the 2026-11-01 window's first 86 min were served by an earlier process).

## Existing state

The abandoned_busy annotation (LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM, landed on `dev`) already annotates post-cancel draining slots — 367 polls / 2.06 % read `abandoned_busy`. The residual class under this item is distinct: a **busy** slot (live prefill) whose live-work fields the status builder leaves empty. The counts-stale shape (`available_slots=2` + `saturated` with fresh detail) is tracked separately in LP-0MVXSX0TZ00798KA and may or may not be the same family (overlap check required before re-measuring).

## Desired change

The status payload for a slot prefilling a real local dispatch must expose its live-work attribution (or an equivalent live-work hint) instead of `saturated` with empty owner/in-flight fields — either in the status builder (`proxy/proxy/observability.py`) or, if root-cause shows the read path is stale, via the residual classifier's widened reason set.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` — capacity hint status builder (live-work attribution during prefill)
- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` — measurement tool / residual classifier
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — slot-polling helpers (multi-slot iteration, per LP-0MRO4U5NT005DP6L)
- `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-11-01_night-post-deploy/verdict.txt` and `saturated_without_live_work_attribution.csv` — evidence (72 rows; 65 mis-attributed to `session_evicted`)
- `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/README.md` — documented `abandoned_busy` semantics (update on behaviour change)

## Risks and assumptions

- (Risk) The `available_slots=2` + `saturated` shape may belong to the counts-stale family (LP-0MVXSX0TZ00798KA); if root-cause confirms overlap, do not duplicate that fix inside this item — link it and keep this item's scope to prefill attribution.
- (Risk) Fixing attribution inside the builder while keeping `saturated` truthful for genuinely busy pools (AC2) is the core tension; existing deterministic tests are the guard.
- (Risk) A re-measurement night with a proxy-process restart inside the window invalidates comparability; pick a restart-free window.
- (Risk) AC4 depends on LP-0MVVXGMGB004DUGR (currently blocked); if it stays blocked, satisfy AC4 via "provably absent" under the widened reason set.
- (Assumption) The 09:06:41 `available_slots=2` + fresh-detail shape is the counts-stale family until proven otherwise.
- (Scope-creep guard) Any additional residual classes discovered during root-cause go to new linked work items, not this item's scope.

## Related work

- discovered-from: LP-0MVUVHBZH007INL1 (verification item whose verdict this files)
- LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM — original draining-slot annotation fix (this is a different residual class)
- LP-0MVVXGMGB004DUGR — attribution extension for unattributable residual polls (reference, do not duplicate)
- LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM — truthful-status contract
- LP-0MVXSX0TZ00798KA — counts-stale family (overlap check required)
- LP-0MRO4U5O1008TLFU / LP-0MRO4U5NT005DP6L — multi-slot polling tests/fix for `poll_slots_for_model()` (completed; polling iteration context)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

No interview required — the item was re-targeted with sufficient evidence by the LP-0MVUVHBZH007INL1 verdict session and the LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM implementation session before this intake. Evidence above is the answer record (log-analysis timestamps and live reproduction 2026-11-02 09:06, sourced from `/var/log/llama-proxy` and the status payloads cited in the Evidence section).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVVXGMGB004DUGR** – Attribute saturated-without-live-work residual polls (blocked)
- **LP-0MRO4U5O1008TLFU** – Write multi-slot tests for poll_slots_for_model() (completed)
- **LP-0MRO4U5NT005DP6L** – Fix poll_slots_for_model() to iterate all slots (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — matched: 0mvutyhg7001s6bm, abandoned, absent, ac1, ac2 (+175 more)
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — matched: 0mvksxr4p001v0cm, 0mvutyhg7001s6bm, abandoned, absent, ac1 (+170 more)
- `proxy/README.md` — matched: 0mvksxr4p001v0cm, abandoned, absent, ac1, ac2 (+166 more)

## Plan (2026-11-02, plan skill)

### Root cause confirmed (log-analysis of `/var/log/llama-proxy`, 2026-11-01/02)

The residual is a **per-session dispatch-record teardown race**, not a stale read
path and not a missing attribution reason:

`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py::_decrement_local_active_queries` closes a *turn*
by writing `local_dispatch_records[(endpoint, session_id)]["active"] = False` and
`expires_at = now + lease_timeout`, logging `lease_renewed`. When the next turn
of the **same session** has already re-acquired that shared record key, the late
teardown of turn N clears turn N+1's live-work attribution for its whole
prefill:

```text
05:31:07,383  Stream finished: ... provider=local session=herdr-1793596937   (turn N ends)
05:31:07,675  [local] POST ... (turn N+1 admitted, same session, same record key)
05:31:08,008  lease_renewed session=herdr-1793596937 timeout=30s            (turn N teardown, LATE)
05:31:13,015  local_active_queries counter recovered: reset from 1 to 0 (0 active dispatch records)
05:31:18,459  status_request avail=1 hint=saturated in_flight=0 owner=None slots_detail_stale=false latency_ms=3000
05:31:18,465  Stream started: provider=local session=herdr-1793596937       (first byte after 10.8 s prefill)
```

Control: polls at `05:33:4x` (same session, prefill with **no** teardown inside
it) read `local_in_flight_requests=1`, `local_owner_session_id=herdr-1793596937-…`.

`_release_local_dispatch` carries the mirror hazard: it `del`s the record
unconditionally, so a late abandonment release can delete a newer dispatch's
record outright.

### Attribution of the 72 residual polls (parent AC4)

- **65/72** (`05:31:18` → `05:33:07`): the cross-turn teardown race above, one
  looping agent session (`herdr-1793596937-…`) whose turn boundaries recur every
  7-18 s. The `session_evicted` cause in the tool's CSV is the 600 s
  nearest-event mis-attribution already documented on LP-0MVUVHBZH007INL1.
- **5/72** ("unattributable"): the **same class**, now attributed:
  `22:12:55,240 [local] POST` → `22:12:55,282 lease_renewed` → polls
  `22:12:57`-`22:13:00`; `23:02:16,450 [local] POST` → `23:02:16,478
  lease_renewed` → poll `23:02:37,677` (`Stream started` `23:02:37,680`);
  `23:03:3x` same shape. AC4 is satisfied by attribution, so this item does not
  depend on the blocked LP-0MVVXGMGB004DUGR.
- **1/72** (`01:28:48`, `available_slots=0`): `prefill_deadline` attribution
  stands.
- Secondary contribution: the status handler samples live-work attribution
  **before** the `/slots` query, so a 3 s poll can pair fresh busy detail with an
  attribution snapshot taken before the dispatch was admitted (the
  `latency_ms=3000` / `2843` rows).

### Deviation from the predicted fix site (documented assumption)

The "Desired change" predicted the fix in `proxy/proxy/observability.py` or in
the residual classifier. Root cause places it in the **dispatch-record
lifecycle** (`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`, a predicted Key File) —
the status builder and the classifier are both reporting the registry correctly.
Fixing the classifier would only annotate a false payload, which the truthful
status contract (LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM) forbids. No producer question is raised:
the goal ("a slot prefilling a real local dispatch must expose its live-work
attribution") is met by the source fix, and AC1/AC2 are unchanged.

### Features (children, test-first, single phase)

| # | Item | Type | Depends on |
|---|------|------|------------|
| 1 | Regression test: late turn teardown must not clear a newer dispatch's attribution | task | — |
| 2 | Scope dispatch teardown to its own dispatch | bug | 1 |
| 3 | Sample live-work attribution after the slot query | bug | 1 |
| 4 | Carry live-work evidence columns in the residual CSV | task | — |
| 4b | Record per-poll attribution for the five 2026-11-01 unattributable polls | task | — |
| 5 | Document per-dispatch live-work attribution semantics | docs | 2, 3 |
| 6 | Re-measure a restart-free night window and record the verdict | task | 2, 3, 4 |

Child ids: 1 `LP-0MVZ3V87D007R6JA`, 2 `LP-0MVZ3V8J1006YGFN`,
3 `LP-0MVZ3V8UR003KCSZ`, 4 `LP-0MVZ3V96D007A825`, 4b `LP-0MVZ3YV7L0056IVL`
(created by the AC-coverage review), 5 `LP-0MVZ3V9HZ0011S44`,
6 `LP-0MVZ3V9T800872B8`.

**Phasing decision:** one phase. The item is Small (~10 h expected) and every
child is a vertical slice of the same observable contract, so no phased rollout
is required; child 6 must run after child 2/3 are deployed to `dev` and served by
a proxy process that starts before the measured window.

### Scope boundary

- The **counts-stale pair** (cache-served `available_slots` alongside a fresh
  `saturated` hint — 71 of the 72 rows also show `available_slots=1` with fresh
  detail) stays with LP-0MVXSX0TZ00798KA. Child 6 reports that figure separately
  and does not claim it fixed here.
- LP-0MVVXGMGB004DUGR (attribution-harness widening) is referenced, not
  duplicated; its AC1 need not be met for this item's AC4.
- `abandoned_busy` semantics are untouched: the residual work is **live**, so it
  must read `saturated` (with attribution), never `abandoned_busy`.
- New residual classes discovered during implementation go to new linked items.

### Key Files (confirmed)

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_try_acquire_local_dispatch`,
  `_decrement_local_active_queries`, `_release_local_dispatch`,
  `_recover_stuck_local_active_queries` (the fix site).
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — `get_llama_local_status` live-work block and the
  slots query that must not precede it.
- `proxy/tests/test_lease_truthfulness.py`, `proxy/tests/test_llama_local_status.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_capacity_signal_verification.py` — guards.
- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`, `scripts/lib/capacity_signals.py` —
  residual CSV evidence columns.
- `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`,
  `proxy/README.md` — documented semantics.
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` — **unchanged** (decision table is correct; it
  is fed a deactivated record).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers (plan session, 2026-11-02)

No producer questions were needed; the item's evidence plus the log analysis
above answered every plan input. Answers recorded here for auditability:

- Q: Where does the attribution loss actually start — the status builder, the
  slot read path, or the dispatch records?
  Answer (engineering, from `/var/log/llama-proxy` for 2026-11-01/02):
  the dispatch records. `_decrement_local_active_queries` deactivates the shared
  per-session record when a turn ends, after the next turn re-acquired it.
  Evidence: `05:31:07,675` POST / `05:31:08,008` `lease_renewed` /
  `05:31:13,015` false counter reset. Final: yes.
- Q: Are the 5 unattributable polls a separate class needing
  LP-0MVVXGMGB004DUGR?
  Answer (engineering, log grep of `proxy.log-2026-11-02_00`): no — all five are
  the same cross-turn teardown class. Final: same class; AC4 satisfied by
  attribution.
- Q: Does fixing this weaken "live work still reads `saturated`"?
  Answer (engineering): no — the fix restores attribution for live work; the
  decision table in `observability.py` is untouched and `abandoned_busy` keeps
  its meaning. Final: contract preserved (parent AC2).

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-02 (plan skill): root-caused the residual to the per-session dispatch
  record teardown race (`_decrement_local_active_queries` /
  `_release_local_dispatch`); confirmed by log evidence for the 65-poll 05:31-05:33
  episode and for all five formerly-unattributable polls. Created 6 feature/test
  children in test-first dependency order; the AC-coverage review auto-created a
  7th (`LP-0MVZ3YV7L0056IVL`) to carry parent AC4's attribution record. Key Files
  corrected: `proxy/proxy/observability.py` is **not** the fix site.

## Problem

The local model backend and the TTS backend are being **SIGKILLed together**, repeatedly, and the kills are not prevented by either mitigation currently deployed. Three events in 6 h 47 min on 2026-11-04, all with the GTT/OOM guard (LP-0MVZ810NG008A3EW, `ce38febf`, live since 2026-11-02) **and** the restart-churn fix (LP-0MVZVZLCS000LQNB, `b2cb86fd`, live since 2026-11-03) loaded in the running proxy (pid 802763, started 2026-11-04T15:33:37Z):

| # | Backend death | Exit | TTS death | Recovered | In-flight dispatch thrown away |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `16:46:35.471` self-heal 1/3 (`restart_reason=llama_server_exit_code_137`) | 137 (SIGKILL) | `16:46:46.752` `exited with code=-9` | 16:46:38 then a **second** attempt 2/3 at 16:46:43, recovered 16:46:47 | 1 `reason=backend_restart` (32 347-token prompt, `elapsed_s=3.1`) |
| 2 | `22:23:19.450` `llama-server process died` → `22:23:24.562 process exited with code 137` | 137 (SIGKILL) | `22:23:18.354` `code=-9`, then **again** `22:23:32.553` | 22:23:22 (backend), TTS on attempt 2/3 at 22:23:35 | — |
| 3 | `22:33:06.675` `llama-server process died` → `22:33:15.372` self-heal 1/3 (`exit_code_137`) | 137 (SIGKILL) | `22:33:09.833` `code=-9` (attempt 1 failed, recovered on 2/3) | 22:33:18 | 1 `reason=backend_restart` (42 246-token prompt, `elapsed_s=3.1`) |

**The churn fix is working as designed** — one or two reasoned self-heal attempts, recovery in 2–14 s, no cascade — so this is *not* a regression of that fix. The problem is that the killer is still running: SIGKILL, delivered to the two GPU-holding processes (llama-server and the TTS server) within seconds of each other, with **no kernel OOM record and no SIGSEGV at those times** (`kern.log`'s last `llama-server` fault is 12:51 on the same day; the 2026-11-02 global-OOM entries are a different, recorded event).

## Why it matters

- **It blocks every ≥24 h measurement window on this host.** The prefill-deadline residual closure (LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I AC3, measurement LP-0MVW8S8OZ00449YR) and the churn-fix validation (LP-0MW0JCFMM0000DM2) both require a restart-free ≥24 h window. At ~3 kills per 7 h the longest clean stretch today was **5 h 37 m** (16:46:47 → 22:23:19); a 24 h window cannot complete while this continues. The window anchors have been re-based five times in three days for exactly this reason.
- **Each kill costs the resident prefix cache** and evicts in-flight dispatches, which is the input to the residual being measured (cold re-prefill, `predicted-warmth` events). Kills therefore *inflate* the residual we are trying to certify.
- **User-visible:** every kill is a mid-turn failure or a remote detour for whoever was generating, plus a cold first byte afterwards (a 40 k–100 k-token prompt re-prefilled at ~43 tok/s).

## Evidence (read-only, reproduced in `/skill:implement LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I`)

- `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.2026-11-04_15` (L26999 `local_eviction_after_acceptance … reason=backend_restart … restart_reason=llama_server_exit_code_137` at 16:46:43) and `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` (22:23 and 22:33 sequences).
- `kern.log`: no OOM at 16:46, 22:23 or 22:33; last `llama-server` `libggml-cpu`/`libamdhip64` fault 12:51 on 2026-11-04.
- Only session live at 22:33 was the v0.1.28 release session, which issued no kill/restart command; no `pkill`/`killall`/`systemctl` invocation appears in any 22:20–22:40 session log.

## Hypotheses to test (not yet evidenced)

1. **GPU-backed host memory (GTT) exhaustion** — the same class as LP-0MVZ810NG008A3EW: both victims are GPU clients (`--n-gpu-layers 80`, `--models-max 2`, `--cache-ram 40960` MB on the model child; the TTS server also runs on the GPU). The 22:23/22:33 deaths each followed a *background model load* (`model=plan`, `model=code`) — loading a second preset while the first is resident is the moment the memory footprint doubles.
2. **systemd-oomd / cgroup kill** — SIGKILL with no kernel OOM record is consistent with oomd; journal retention on this host is short (~20 min) so the oomd record may simply be gone; needs `journalctl -u systemd-oomd` capture at the time of the next event (or persisting the journal).
3. **Launcher-side kill** — `start-llama.sh`/`start-proxy.sh` cleanup paths were hardened in LP-0MVZ810NG008A3EW (`_kill_matching`, self-match exclusion); a residual launcher kill path would need to be proven, not assumed.

## Scope

**In:** capture the killer (persist the journal / sample `gpu_active`+`MemAvailable`+`oom_score_adj`+cgroup memory at second resolution), confirm or refute hypothesis 1, and stop the kills (bound GTT usage, prevent a second-model autoload while one is resident, or protect the processes via the systemd unit's `OOMScoreAdjust`). Also record `restart_reason` coverage for the TTS path (it currently reports only `code=-9`).

**Out:** the prefill-deadline residual measurement itself (LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I / LP-0MVW8S8OZ00449YR) — this item only unblocks its window.

## Duplicate check (2026-11-04)

Searched `SIGKILL exit 137`, `out of memory oom`, `TTS killed`, `host memory pressure`, `restart churn`. LP-0MVZ810NG008A3EW (global OOM, GPU GTT) and LP-0MVZVZLCS000LQNB (restart churn) are both `completed` as "Shipped in v0.1.28"; their fixes are live and are demonstrably not preventing these three kills, so this is a **recurrence with mitigations live**, not a duplicate of either. LP-0MW0JCFMM0000DM2 validates the churn fix over a restart-free window — it consumes this item's outcome rather than duplicating it.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Killer identified or bounded.** Either the killing agent is named with its own log/config evidence (kernel, oomd, cgroup, launcher), or the kill window's memory state is captured at second resolution for the next event (`gpu_active` / GTT, `MemAvailable`, per-process RSS, cgroup limits, `oom_score_adj`) and the leading hypothesis is confirmed or refuted.
- **AC2 — Kills stop.** ≥24 h with **zero** `llama_server_exit_code_137`, zero `llama-server process died` and zero `TTS server exited with code=-9` events, with the evidence recorded.
- **AC3 — Protection recorded.** The surviving protection (cgroup limit / `OOMScoreAdjust` / autoload bound / supervisor) is documented with the command or config that sets it, plus the operator runbook entry.
- **AC4 — Window hand-off.** The ≥24 h restart-free anchor produced by AC2 is recorded on LP-0MVZ2EPI3006Y0WN and LP-0MVW8S8OZ00449YR so the residual measurement can finally run.

---

## Intake (2026-11-05) — fresh evidence, reframed premise

Read-only observation; **no code change** was made. This section updates the
2026-11-04 premise: the dominant death signature is now **GPU-library faults**, not
an OOM/SIGKILL with no kernel record.

### Fresh evidence (2026-11-05)

| Signal | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `llama-server` GPU-library faults, 2026-11-05 | **16** | `/var/log/kern.log` |
| `llama-server` GPU-library faults, 2026-11-04 | **22** | `/var/log/kern.log` |
| `Out of memory: Killed process … llama-server`, 2026-11-05 | **0** | `/var/log/kern.log` |
| Proxy `watchdog detected llama-server exit code=` | **84 events, all `137`; zero `139`** | `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*` |
| `restart_reason` values (all rotations) | `llama_server_exit_code_137` ×133, `backend_unreachable` ×4 | proxy logs |
| TTS deaths | `TTS server exited with code=-9` (≈105 across rotations) | proxy logs |
| `systemd-oomd` kill records | **none** (journal retains from 2026-03-25) | `journalctl -u systemd-oomd`, `journalctl --grep` |
| Host memory | `MemAvailable` ≈ **81 GiB** / 124 GiB; swap 753 MiB / 8 GiB (9 %) | `free -h` |
| GTT | **34.9 GiB used**, 137 GiB pool, **28 % of physical RAM** (warn 50 %, critical 65 %) | `mem_info_gtt_*` |
| PSI memory | `some avg10=0.00`, `full avg10=0.00` | `/proc/pressure/memory` |
| `oom_score_adj` on running backend, TTS, proxy | **0 for all** (code intends backend `+800`, proxy `-900`) | `/proc/<pid>/oom_score_adj` |

Fault signatures (all `/var/log/kern.log`):

```text
llama-server[..]: segfault at .. ip .. in libggml-cpu.so.0.9.11[51048,..]
traps: llama-server[..] general protection fault ip:.. in libamdhip64.so.7.2.70204[2b931f,..]
```

Running backend: `version 8782 (e97492369)`; `libggml-cpu.so.0.9.11` md5
`3d1fe87a…` with **37 `_generic` kernels and 0 arch-specific** ones. Same artifact and
same offsets (`0x51048` / `0x51057`, inside `ggml_cpu_extra_work_size`) that the
sibling diagnosis pinned to a **llama.cpp CPU-backend repack / `tensor_traits` vtable
dereference** on `LP-0MW0JCFMM0000DM2` (AC5) and `LP-0MVZVZLCS000LQNB`.

### Effect on the hypotheses above

1. **GTT / host-memory exhaustion — refuted for today's events.** GTT is at 28 % of
   physical RAM with zero memory pressure; the 2026-11-02 global OOM is a *different,
   recorded* event.
2. **`systemd-oomd` / cgroup kill — not evidenced.** oomd is active but has logged no
   kills; journal retention is long, so "the record may be gone" no longer holds.
3. **Launcher-side kill / self-inflicted `137` — strongest lead.** The proxy reports
   `exit 137` for *every* death while the kernel reports `SIGSEGV`/`GPF` (`139`), and
   TTS dies with `-9` in lockstep. Consistent with the proxy's own process-group
   `SIGKILL` escalation during restart/shutdown, or one external group signal — and
   with the real fault being masked. The `137`-vs-`139` mismatch must be explained
   before choosing a fix.
4. **OOM protection is not actually applied.** All running GPU processes carry
   `oom_score_adj=0`; the code intends `+800` on the backend. The proxy half is
   expected to fail unprivileged (logged 5×), but the backend half is missing,
   including for the router child the proxy does not directly spawn.

### Refreshed acceptance criteria (supersede the section above)

- **AC1 — Deaths correctly attributed.** Either the killing agent is named with its own
  evidence (kernel, oomd, cgroup, launcher, or proxy process-group escalation), **or**
  the next kill window is captured at second resolution (`gpu_active`/GTT,
  `MemAvailable`, per-process RSS, cgroup `memory.events`, `oom_score_adj`) and the
  `exit-137`-vs-`SIGSEGV(139)` discrepancy is explained. Repeating the OOM hypothesis
  does not satisfy AC1.
- **AC2 — Kills stop.** ≥24 h with zero `llama_server_exit_code_137`, zero
  `llama-server process died`, zero `TTS server exited with code=-9`, and zero
  `llama-server[…]: segfault|general protection fault` lines, with evidence recorded.
- **AC3 — Root cause fixed or bounded.** The `libggml-cpu` repack fault and the
  `libamdhip64` GPF are fixed (e.g. rebuild with arch-specific kernels / disable the
  repack extra-buffer-type path) or bounded so they cannot take down the backend; the
  mitigation is documented with the exact command/config.
- **AC4 — Observability corrected.** The backend/TTS death record reports the true
  termination signal and restart reason (not a blanket `137`); the TTS path carries a
  `restart_reason` (currently only `code=-9`).
- **AC5 — OOM protection verified.** The backend (including the router child) carries
  the intended raised `oom_score_adj`, verified from `/proc`, or the gap is recorded
  with its reason.
- **AC6 — Window hand-off.** The ≥24 h restart-free anchor from AC2 is recorded on
  `LP-0MVZEPI3006Y0WN` and `LP-0MVW8S8OZ00449YR`.
- **AC7 — Tests and docs.** The changed-scope test gate and the full project test
  suite pass with the change; related documentation (runbook and any
  segfault/observability notes under `docs/`) is updated. (CHANGELOG excluded — owned by
  the ship pipeline.)

### Duplicate check (2026-11-05)

Searched `SIGKILL`, `libamdhip64`, `oomd`, `segfault`, `repack`,
`ggml_cpu_extra_work_size`. **Partial overlap, not duplicates:**

- `LP-0MW0JCFMM0000DM2` — a *validation/measurement* task that already holds the
  verified `libggml-cpu` repack diagnosis (AC5). It consumes this item's outcome; it
  does not own the fix.
- `LP-0MVZVZLCS000LQNB` — *bounding* the self-heal loop (completed). This item covers
  the deaths themselves, not the loop bound.
- `LP-0MVZ810NG008A3EW` — the earlier global OOM (completed). Its fix is live and
  demonstrably does not prevent these deaths.

### Related work

- `LP-0MVZ810NG008A3EW` — global OOM / GPU GTT exhaustion (completed; fix live).
- `LP-0MVZVZLCS000LQNB` — llama-server restart churn (completed; bounded).
- `LP-0MW0JCFMM0000DM2` — validates the churn fix; holds the repack diagnosis.
- `LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I` — residual 120 s deadline evictions (blocked by this item).
- `LP-0MVW8S8OZ00449YR` — post-change ≥24 h measurement (blocked).
- `LP-0MVZEPI3006Y0WN` — window anchor.
- `LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2` — epic blocked by this item.
- `LP-0MQOAQEFP004WD0V` — prior ROCm/HIP crash fix (completed; GPFs persist).
- `LP-0MS9H56R9000RIYF` — established no oomd/OOM kills for an earlier round.
- `LP-0MVZT9L3N001XABB` — orphan-adoption prerequisite.

### Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — misattributed root cause.** The original `SIGKILL` framing may point the fix
  at OOM/cgroup protection when the real cause is a CPU-backend segfault. AC1 forbids
  repeating the OOM hypothesis.
- **Risk — self-inflicted `137`.** If the proxy's own process-group `SIGKILL` is the
  source, "fixing the killer" means fixing restart hygiene. AC1 must distinguish it.
- **Risk — GPU driver/distro coupling.** The `libamdhip64` GPF may be a ROCm 7.2
  userland/kernel mismatch that a rebuild does not solve.
- **Risk — window invalidation.** Any restart during evidence gathering re-bases the
  ≥24 h anchor. Prefer read-only capture; coordinate restarts with
  `LP-0MVZEPI3006Y0WN`.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Residual measurement, churn validation and epic progress are
  separate items; record follow-ups as linked work items.
- **Assumption —** the `kern.log` faults and the `exit 137` proxy events are the *same*
  deaths, pending AC1.
- **Assumption —** the host remains the single-node `sorra-agents-1` APU (`gfx1151`),
  so `LP-0MVZ810NG008A3EW` GTT semantics still apply.

## Appendix: clarifying questions (OPEN — producer input required)

Each has the agent's recommended option; the recommendation is advisory only.

- **Q1 — Scope of this item.**
  Given today's evidence (SIGSEGV in the `ggml` repack path plus `libamdhip64` GPF,
  zero OOM), should this item own the **root-cause fix** (rebuild llama.cpp with
  arch-specific kernels / avoid the repack path), or remain a **capture-and-bound**
  item?
  Options: (a) own the root-cause fix; (b) capture-only and spin a child for the fix;
  (c) close as covered by `LP-0MW0JCFMM0000DM2`.
  **Recommended:** (a) — the cause and a candidate fix are already identified, and a
  capture-only item cannot satisfy AC2. Source: agent research, 2026-11-05; pending
  producer answer.
- **Q2 — Observability fix in scope?**
  The proxy reports `exit 137` for every death while the kernel reports SIGSEGV/GPF
  (139). Should fixing the exit-code/`restart_reason` reporting (and giving TTS a
  `restart_reason`) be part of this item?
  Options: (a) yes, in scope; (b) separate item; (c) out of scope.
  **Recommended:** (a) — AC1/AC4 depend on an accurate death record. Source: agent
  research; pending producer answer.
- **Q3 — OOM-protection verification in scope?**
  All running GPU processes show `oom_score_adj=0` (code intends backend `+800`).
  Should verifying/reapplying backend OOM protection (including the router child) be
  in scope?
  Options: (a) yes, small addition; (b) separate item; (c) out of scope.
  **Recommended:** (a) — the "mitigation live" premise depends on it. Source: agent
  research; pending producer answer.

## Summary

A single reusable "busy engine" test harness: a stubbed `/slots` that outlasts both proxy poll budgets (counts 2.0 s, detail `STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT` 1.0 s), used to reproduce the intake's measured degradation deterministically. Every later feature in this plan asserts against this harness rather than inventing its own stub, so the same busy-engine conditions hold across the whole plan.

## Why test-first

The intake measured the defect on a live engine. Without a deterministic reproduction each later fix is unverifiable, and the AC1 "< 5 % of polls stale" target cannot be measured in CI.

**Key Files:**
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_busy_engine_policy.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_failure_graceful_degradation.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_detail_cache_fallback.py`
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py`
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test with a stubbed `/slots` whose latency exceeds the current timeouts reproduces the degradation: `slot_counts_stale=true`, `slots_detail_stale=true`, `slots_stale=true` on `/llama/local/status`.
- The harness exposes one configurable fake `/slots` fixture (delay, status code, payload) that later features reuse; no later feature adds a second stub mechanism.
- The degraded poll still returns a well-formed payload inside a bounded wall clock — the endpoint never waits for counts plus detail serially beyond the documented budget.
- The baseline assertion is recorded so the pre-change behaviour is provably reproduced: the test fails if the stub stops exceeding the budgets.
- Tests run in the existing proxy test suite and pass through the test skill.

## Minimal implementation

- Add `proxy/tests/test_slots_busy_engine_policy.py` with an asyncio-gated slow-`/slots` fixture parameterised by delay, status code and payload.
- Drive `get_llama_local_status()` through the same FastAPI test-client pattern the existing slots tests use.
- Assert the three staleness flags, the payload shape and a bounded latency.
- Document the fixture in a module docstring so the detail, ETA, abandonment and policy features import it rather than copy it.

## Reuse (verified in the tree)

- `test_slots_failure_graceful_degradation.py`, `test_slots_detail_cache_fallback.py` and `test_slots_poll_coalescing.py` already stub `/slots`; extend their fixture pattern instead of adding a parallel one.
- `_query_slots` (2.0 s) and `_query_slots_detail(timeout=STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT)` in the status handler define the budgets under test.

# Test: launch-authority and live-backend assertions (red first)

**Parent:** LP-0MW1VDZTC00034S7 · **Type:** task (tests) · **Phase 1 of 8**

## Context

The proxy's restart/adoption path trusts `proxy/.llama_server_signature.json` and
never inspects the *live* backend. On 2026-11-04 a hand-launched container
(`--parallel 1`, no `--slot-save-path`, log inside the container) was adopted
silently, and the lifecycle then spawned six defunct host-side `llama-server`
children against the container-held port. No existing test pins any of this.

## Scope (tests only — expected to fail until the implementation items land)

Cover, in `proxy/tests/test_launch_authority.py` and
`proxy/tests/test_slot_persistence_policy.py`:

1. Listener on `server.llama_server_port` that the lifecycle did not start
   (host pid): inspection reports `foreign`, port, pid, resolved slot count and
   the live `--parallel` value.
2. Container holder: podman is mocked; inspection reports the container name,
   its init pid, and the in-container `--parallel`/`--slot-save-path`.
3. No listener: inspection reports `absent` and raises nothing.
4. Signature matches **and** live `--parallel` equals
   `server.session_slot_pool_size`: adoption is allowed.
5. Signature matches but live `--parallel` differs from
   `session_slot_pool_size`: mismatch verdict; the backend is not adopted and
   local dispatch is refused.
6. Port pre-occupied by a foreign holder: `start_llama_server()` does **not**
   call `subprocess.Popen` (assert zero spawn attempts, i.e. no defunct
   children).
7. Log-liveness fixture where the log stops growing: the check reports an
   error and `/health` exposes it.
8. `slot_save` returning 501: exactly one WARNING and no further save attempts;
   200: no disable; no `--slot-save-path` on the live server: saves never
   attempted.

No test may spawn or kill a real OS process (follow
`proxy/tests/test_lifecycle_spawn.py` conventions: everything mocked).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Startup detects a llama-server the lifecycle did not start (host or container) and reports it explicitly, including the port, pid/container and the resolved slot count.
- [ ] No defunct host-side `llama-server` processes are produced when a container holds the port (test drives the lifecycle with the port pre-occupied).
- [ ] A liveness check proves the proxy can read fresh llama-server output; a fixture where the log stops growing raises a visible error, and a test asserts the condition is not silently reported as "no samples".
- [ ] `slot_save` either returns 200 (path configured) or is not attempted; a test pins whichever behaviour is chosen, and a 501 is never logged as a routine warning.
- [ ] The new test modules fail against the current code (red baseline recorded in a comment) and pass once the implementation children land.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add the two test modules using `MagicMock`/`monkeypatch` for `subprocess.Popen`,
  `podman`, `/proc` reads and `httpx` slot endpoints.
- Reuse `_find_free_port()`-style helpers; never bind the real `8080`.
- Record the red baseline (`python3 -m pytest <module> -q` output) in a comment
  before handing over.

## Key Files

- `proxy/tests/test_launch_authority.py` (new)
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_persistence_policy.py` (new)
- `proxy/tests/test_lifecycle_spawn.py` (conventions to follow)
- `proxy/tests/test_log_relay_adoption.py` (log-path fixtures to reuse)

## Dependencies

None — this is the first item in the phase order.

Test-first slice for AC7 (nightly report shows improvement) and AC9 (effectiveness section). Freezes the pre-change baseline and lands the red tests the renderer slice turns green.

## Goal

A committed, reproducible baseline for every AC9 field, plus failing tests for the new `## Residency retention effectiveness` report section.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A committed baseline fixture/doc records, for the reference window **2026-11-01 11:09:07 → 2026-11-02 11:09:07** (the window the item was created from), each AC9 field: measured-ratio share **0.7 %** (13,950 of 14,043 decisions unmeasured; 58.0 % `unavailable:no_slot`, 39.2 % `unavailable:stale_view`), resident admits vs evicted denials, **254** post-acceptance evictions, local tokens processed **37,954,924**, GPU busy **66.4 %**, plus the exact command that reproduces each figure.
- [ ] A test asserts the report renders a `## Residency retention effectiveness` section containing all nine AC9 fields (measured-ratio share, resident admits, evicted denials, post-acceptance evictions by cause, within-budget ETA/deadline refusals, `resident_prefix_insufficient` skips, wasted prefill tokens, local tokens processed) and their baseline column.
- [ ] A test asserts the section is **additive**: the `summary_to_json` key set is a superset of the pre-change key set (no existing key renamed/removed/retyped).
- [ ] Tests fail (red) before the renderer slice lands; the red run is recorded in a work-item comment.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Re-run the parser/aggregation over the reference window fixtures and pin the derived numbers in a fixture module under `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/` (no live log dependency in CI).
2. Add the two tests next to the existing residency/post-acceptance-eviction report tests.
3. Record baselines in the item comment so the follow-up measurement item (LP-0MVZ9U8E7007AXPL) can cite them.

**Key Files:**
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_post_acceptance_eviction_report.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_performance_metrics_section.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py`
- `docs/dev/resident-prefix-rollout.md`

**Definition of Done:** tests committed red-first; `/skill:test` changed-scope run recorded; build → changed-scope tests → commit order respected.

**Dependencies:** none. Blocks the report-renderer slice.
data.title: Residency retention baseline capture and report effectiveness tests

data.description:
discovered-from:LP-0MVV29XDW006VTWK

## Finding

The proxy's log retention (7 days: `logging.retention_days` default in
`proxy/proxy/utils.py:1034`, which makes `TimedRotatingFileHandler` keep
`backupCount = 7 × 24 / 6 = 28` six-hour segments, with `/etc/logrotate.d/llama-proxy`
as a `rotate 7` daily safety net) is shorter than the age a committed
measurement record reaches before it is audited or re-examined.

Concrete instance: `LP-0MVV29XDW006VTWK` had to restate the pre-change baseline
on the window `2026-10-28 00:10:18` → `2026-10-29 00:10:18` (8 days before the
implementing session). The window was measured in full on 2026-10-30, but by
2026-11-05 the first ~16 h of `2026-10-28` had been pruned: only
`proxy.log.2026-10-28_16.gz` (16:16:14→22:16:12) and
`proxy.log.2026-10-29_001015.gz` (00:00:00→00:10:15) survive — **6 h 10 m of a
24 h window (25.7 %, 67 of 136 enqueued waits)**. The committed record
therefore carries two provenance classes (measurement-time full window vs
today's coverage re-measurement) instead of a single regenerable artefact.

This is a recurring shape, not a one-off: any "measure a window, then commit a
record" slice that lands more than ~7 days after its window has to be
documented as un-reproducible, and every AC of the form "re-running the
embedded command regenerates the committed JSON" degrades to "regenerable
while the archives survive".

## Goal (user story)

As the LLM proxy operator, I want a measurement window to stay re-derivable for
at least as long as the records that quote it, so a committed record can be
re-checked by a later session instead of being taken on trust.

## Options (not a decision — intake should choose)

1. **Raise `logging.retention_days`** (e.g. 7→14 or 30). Cheap in disk: measured
   on 2026-11-05, `/var/log/llama-proxy` holds 46 `proxy.log*.gz` archives
   totalling **42 MB** (≈0.9 MB per six-hour segment), so doubling or
   quadrupling retention costs tens of MB, not GB. The knob already exists
   (`logging.retention_days`). Costs: more files in one directory (check
   `prune_logs` startup scan time) and the logrotate drop-in's `rotate 7`
   safety net must be raised to match, or it will prune what the in-process
   handler retains.
2. **Archive the window's archives with the record** — a `--emit-archives`
   mode or a documented `tar`/`rsync` step alongside a record commit. Larger
   repo footprint (or an external artefact store), but makes the record
   self-contained forever.
3. **Record the harness output as the artefact of authority** and drop the
   "regenerates byte-for-byte" expectation from records older than retention —
   documentation-only, no code change; what `LP-0MVV29XDW006VTWK` does today.

## Acceptance criteria (draft, for intake)

- AC1: A documented retention window is at least as long as the longest-lived
  measurement record the project commits, with the value stated in
  `docs/dev/` and pinned by a test.
- AC2: A measurement record older than the retention window is either
  reproducible from a committed/archived artefact, or the record states its
  provenance classes explicitly (no silent re-derivation claim).
- AC3: Disk cost of the chosen retention is measured, not assumed, and stated
  on the host-install/retention doc.

## Evidence

- `docs/dev/prefill-admission-conversion-diurnal-baseline.md`
  ("Provenance and coverage") — the coverage map and the pruning mechanism.
- `proxy/proxy/utils.py` (`setup_logging`, `prune_logs`,
  `logging.retention_days` default 7).
- `/etc/logrotate.d/llama-proxy` (`rotate 7`, `size`-free daily safety net).
- `scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py` — rotation/decompression discovery (unaffected;
  the loss is retention, not discovery).
data.title: Proxy log retention (7 days) is shorter than the records that quote measured windows

question: Intake (2026-11-05) needs producer scope confirmation — the fresh evidence reframes the premise (see description 'Intake (2026-11-05)' section). Three questions, each with an advisory recommendation:

**Q1 — Scope of this item.** Given today's evidence (SIGSEGV in the ggml repack path and libamdhip64 GPF; zero OOM, zero oomd kills), should this item own the root-cause fix (rebuild llama.cpp with arch-specific kernels / avoid the repack extra-buffer-type path), or remain a capture-and-bound item? Options: (a) own the root-cause fix; (b) capture-only, spin a child for the fix; (c) close as covered by LP-0MW0JCFMM0000DM2. **Recommended: (a)** — the cause and a candidate fix are already identified and a capture-only item cannot satisfy AC2 (kills stop).

**Q2 — Observability fix in scope?** The proxy logs exit code=137 for every death while the kernel logs SIGSEGV/GPF (139). Should fixing the exit-code/restart_reason reporting (and giving TTS a restart_reason; today it reports only code=-9) be part of this item? Options: (a) yes, in scope; (b) separate item; (c) out of scope. **Recommended: (a)** — AC1/AC4 depend on an accurate death record.

**Q3 — OOM-protection verification in scope?** All running GPU processes (backend, TTS, proxy) show oom_score_adj=0, while the code intends backend +800. Should verifying/reapplying backend OOM protection (including the router child the proxy does not directly spawn) be in scope? Options: (a) yes, small addition; (b) separate item; (c) out of scope. **Recommended: (a)** — the item's 'mitigation live' premise depends on it.

Key verified facts behind the questions: 16 llama-server GPU-library faults on 2026-11-05 and 22 on 2026-11-04 in /var/log/kern.log; 0 OOM kills; 84 proxy events all 'exit code=137' and zero '139'; GTT at 28% of physical RAM with PSI memory pressure 0; no systemd-oomd kill records (journal retains from 2026-03-25).
